Real bubble is in VC land with private companies like Instinct… $10B valuations off 100k users while $SNAP is worth less with close to 1 Billion MAU. 

Supply chain stocks aren’t a bubble though, if anything names like $AAOI and others are very undervalued relative to forward growth. 

And you have demand visibility from hyperscalers extending multiple years…

Hyperscalers are the ones ultimately funding the AI buildout. As seen with $AMZN to $GOOGL earnings commentary, the ROI is seen as wildly attractive.

Even $MSFT said they’d be FCF positive during the buildout period. 

I was more worried about counterparty risk until OpenAI went out and raised like $168B recently.

At the very start of my grad school in 2005, I wrote paper about the original computer hacking/phreaking/BBS scene: hackers were often driven by curiosity but the tools they made were widely exploited by "Script Kiddies" who caused most damage & chaos

Anyhow, about AI hacking...
This document is going to be an assigned reading in college classes that cover this moment in time, there's a lot happening in a few paragraphs... https://www.ahmath.org/statements

Interesting to see, given the controversy over the OpenAI release of a series of proofs and what it means for the discipline of mathematics, that at least some of the OpenAI proofs seem to have kicked off extremely rapid iterative advances from a wide community of collaborators.

quoted_tweet.text:
Validated and merged Rohan's PR. Big gain on a really difficult regime (that frankly I was stuck at). Incredible work.

κ = 2⁻¹⁵  (tightened from κ = 2⁻¹⁸²)

A 500 thousand fold improvement over the previous result and a 2 ^ 167 fold improvement over the original OpenAI result.

This result was a true community effort that combined techniques from a number of contributors. I want to take time to highlight each of them, but for now getting these results verified and published as fast as possible so everyone working on the problem is at the leading edge.
